sentences.text: The holotype specimen — the specific fossil the species is based on — contains parts of the spine, ribs, a thigh bone, finger bones, and many bony plates.
Its thigh bone measures exactly 46 centimeters in length.
A pelvic shield formed by fused plates displays a unique rosette pattern where central elements lack a full ring of smaller neighbors.
The body armor includes thin triangular plates ranging from 10 to 35 centimeters long, alongside domed and cone-shaped varieties.
Scientists including Rongjun Chen and Wenjie Zheng formally named and described this genus in 2013.
Researchers classify Dongyangopelta within the clade Nodosauridae, a group of armored dinosaurs, based on the separation of the femoral head from the great trochanter.
Phylogenetic analysis places it in a polytomy — a branching point with unresolved relationships — with Sauroplites and Taohelong at the base of Nodosauridae.
This animal lived during the Albian to Cenomanian stages, approximately 113.2 to 93.9 million years ago.
